subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A straight line with slope 1 passes through Q(−3,5) meets the line x+y−6=0 at P. Find the distance PQ.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.63 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 58.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 22 · TS 15. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the SAME CHAPTER prints 1+1+2 on answer 59 (book p.63), and this answer is cut to the same shape — the two setting-up moves at one mark each and the closing work at two. Where an answer's own shape is four equal moves instead, 1+1+1+1 is used and this note says so. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. NOTE: The Straight Line is the FIRST Maths-1B unit to occupy ALL THREE sections of the paper — the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.3) gives it 2+2 marks in Section A, 4 in Section B and 7 in Section C, 15 in all, tying Differentiation as the highest-scoring unit on the paper. It therefore has three separate chapters in this book: LAQ chapter 1 (book pp.14-18), SAQ chapter 9 (pp.61-64) and VSAQ chapter 14 (pp.79-82). recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the parametric form gives you, and what r means at the end.

steps.label: Find the angle
steps.margin_note: First mark. The parametric form needs an ANGLE, not a slope, so convert whatever the question gives into θ before anything else.
steps.memory_tip: Slope 1 means tan θ = 1, so θ = 45° — the parametric form needs the angle, not the slope.

recall.must_convey: That the given information is converted into the angle θ the line makes with the X-axis.
accept: convert the given slope or direction into the angle theta
the parametric form needs the angle not the slope
find theta from tan theta equals the slope
slope nunchi theta teesukovali
get the angle with the X axis

steps.why: The parametric form measures distance ALONG the line, and distance needs a direction — which is what θ supplies.
common_mistakes: Using the slope directly in place of cosθ and sinθ.
Taking θ as the angle with the Y-axis.

steps.label: Write the parametric point
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Any point at distance r from Q along the line is (x₁ + r cosθ, y₁ + r sinθ). Writing P this way turns an unknown POINT into a single unknown NUMBER.
steps.memory_tip: Write P as (x₁ + r cos θ, y₁ + r sin θ), turning the unknown point into a single number r.
lines: Given point Q(x₁, y₁) = (−3, 5) and distance PQ = r, then
P = (x₁ + r cosθ, y₁ + r sinθ)

recall.must_convey: That P is written as (x₁ + r cosθ, y₁ + r sinθ) with the given point and angle.
accept: P is x one plus r cos theta comma y one plus r sin theta
write the point in parametric form with distance r
the parametric point at distance r from Q
parametric form lo P ni rayali
use x one plus r cos theta

steps.why: One unknown r replaces two unknown coordinates, which is the whole advantage of the parametric form over the ordinary one.
common_mistakes: Swapping cosθ and sinθ between the two coordinates.
Leaving r out of one of the two coordinates.

steps.label: Put it on the line
steps.margin_note: Third mark. P is stated to lie on the given line, so its coordinates satisfy that equation. Substituting produces one equation in r alone.
steps.memory_tip: P is on the given line, so substituting gives one equation in r.
lines: But P lies on the line x + y − 6 = 0 ⇒ x + y = 6

recall.must_convey: That P's parametric coordinates are substituted into the line P lies on.
accept: substitute the parametric point into the line equation
P lies on the line so put its coordinates in
this gives one equation in r
P line meeda undi kabatti substitute cheyyali
put the parametric point into the given line

steps.why: Everything before this was setting up; this is the step that actually uses the line P sits on.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that BOTH coordinates carry r/√2, so the two r-terms add.

steps.label: Solve for r
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The distance PQ IS r, so solving for r finishes the question with no extra work.
steps.memory_tip: PQ is r itself — no extra work after solving.

recall.must_convey: That solving gives 2√2, which is the distance PQ.
accept: solve for r and that is the distance P Q
r is the distance so the answer comes straight out
simplify to get r
r ye distance kabatti answer adi
the distance P Q is this

steps.why: r was DEFINED as the distance along the line, so no distance formula is ever needed — that is why the parametric form is the right tool here.
common_mistakes: Finding P's coordinates and then applying the distance formula, which wastes time.
Leaving r negative when the question asks for a distance.

insider_note: Slope 1 means θ = 45°, so cosθ and sinθ are both 1/√2 and the two r-terms add. Leave the answer as 2√2 — the parametric r IS the distance, so no distance formula is needed at the end.
